name: Bullet

business_model.summary: Bullet is a fast coding agent for software developers, currently offered for free with no clear monetization model mentioned.

evidence.quote: Free to use. No subscriptions. Just a faster way to ship.
A Faster Coding Agent

team.summary: Founded by Adi and Alex, who started the company in their senior year dorm after working at AppLovin and Citadel.

evidence.quote: We’re Adi and Alex, founders of Bullet, a faster coding agent.
Bullet started in a senior year dorm. We were fresh out of working at AppLovin and Citadel
We were going to use our skills optimizing stock pricing calculation speeds and agent document context

product.summary: A fast coding agent and harness that optimizes speed by reducing round trips, parallelizing independent tool calls, routing models, and performing targeted code search.

evidence.quote: Bullet routes, searches, and executes with one purpose: keeping up with you.
On SWE-bench Verified, Bullet resolved 479/500 (95.8%) in one attempt, averaging 119s per task
the biggest insight was that model speed matters less than reducing round trips.

competitors.summary: Competes with existing coding agents and harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, maki.sh, and pellmell.ai.

evidence.quote: Let’s take on Claude Code and Codex, we can do it!
I guess I can fund raise just by having built https://maki.sh
evidence.author: tontinton

evidence.quote: I would stick to OpenCode.
evidence.author: esafak

why_now.summary: Developers are increasingly frustrated by the slow execution speeds and high costs of existing coding agents.

evidence.quote: We were spending hours waiting for coding agents like Claude Code and Codex, and got so frustrated
At our company, we were burning hours waiting on agent runs.

risks.risk: History of frequent pivots (six pivots before this product) which may indicate a lack of long-term focus.

evidence.quote: Bullet started as an AI hedge fund, a browser-use agent, synthetic financial data (oof), a mobile IDE, and a bunch of other things.
Is there another pivot coming? This would make me nervous.
evidence.author: throw03172019

risks.risk: Security and trust issues due to closed-source distribution requiring root access.

evidence.quote: Installing a .deb requires root. Okay, a coding agent that wants root access.
evidence.author: lrvick

evidence.quote: Proprietary software is no longer a moat, and for something like this it just makes your software very hard to trust.
evidence.author: lrvick

risks.risk: Low defensibility as a harness that can be easily replicated or built via prompting.

evidence.quote: I'm genuinely confused about what is mechanically different in this harness that could not be accomplished with a prompt/skill in another harness.
evidence.author: yetanotherjosh

evidence.quote: nobody would use it because they’d just point their own AI at it and clone it. It’s just not that hard.
evidence.author: lowbloodsugar

founder_depth.why: The founders have technical backgrounds from AppLovin and Citadel, but they are fresh out of college (dorm room startup) and have pivoted six times without prior exits or deep domain depth in AI research.

evidence.quote: Bullet started in a senior year dorm. We were fresh out of working at AppLovin and Citadel

shipping_evidence.why: The product is live with macOS, Linux, and Windows builds, a CLI, and published SWE-bench results, but the code is closed-source and there is no public GitHub repository.

evidence.quote: DOWNLOAD FOR MAC 1.4.17
npm install -g @trybullet/cli

demand_signal.why: Solid HN engagement with some active users praising the speed, but many commenters are highly skeptical of the benchmark validity and the value of a proprietary harness.

evidence.quote: I recently switched over to using primarily Bullet for my projects and the speed of it makes it very nice
evidence.author: lucasdimarco

evidence.quote: I think this adds no value. I would stick to OpenCode.
evidence.author: esafak

defensibility.why: The product is a closed-source harness/wrapper around existing LLMs, which commenters note is easy to replicate, clone, or replace with custom prompts and open-source alternatives.

evidence.quote: Proprietary software is no longer a moat
evidence.author: lrvick

evidence.quote: nobody would use it because they’d just point their own AI at it and clone it. It’s just not that hard.
evidence.author: lowbloodsugar

analysis.case_summary: The strongest point for Bullet is its impressive speed and high SWE-bench score (95.8%), while the strongest point against is its lack of defensibility as a closed-source agent harness that users can easily replicate or replace with open-source alternatives.
would_change_my_mind: Evidence of paying enterprise customers willing to pay for a proprietary agent harness.
A detailed technical breakdown proving their parallel execution and context hygiene cannot be easily replicated via prompting in open-source harnesses.
Open-sourcing the core agent loop to resolve developer trust and security concerns while maintaining a monetization strategy.
data_gaps: No information on how the company plans to generate revenue or monetize the product.
No details on the exact model providers supported or how API costs are handled.
No public GitHub repository or source code to verify security and implementation details.
